title: Continuation-extensionality of the term sub-tree
statement: Let $\ell$ be a list of literals on $n$ variables and let $\rho$ be a restriction. For a continuation $c : \mathrm{Restriction}\,n \to \mathrm{DecisionTree}\,n$, write $T(\ell, \rho, c)$ for the term sub-tree built from $\ell$ starting at $\rho$ with continuation $c$. If two continuations $c_1$ and $c_2$ agree on every restriction $\rho'$ whose number of free variables is at most the number of free variables of $\rho$ — that is, $c_1(\rho') = c_2(\rho')$ whenever $\rho'$ has no more free variables than $\rho$ — then $T(\ell, \rho, c_1) = T(\ell, \rho, c_2)$.
hypotheses_covered: lits is a list of literals on n variables
cont1, cont2 are two continuations from restrictions to decision trees
cont1 and cont2 agree on every restriction with at most as many free variables as rho
replaced:
If two continuations $\mathrm{cont}_1, \mathrm{cont}_2$ agree on all restrictions $\rho'$ with
$\rho'.\mathrm{numFree} \le \rho.\mathrm{numFree}$, then $\mathrm{termSubTree}\,\mathit{lits}\,\rho\,\mathrm{cont}_1 = \mathrm{termSubTree}\,\mathit{lits}\,\rho\,\mathrm{cont}_2$.
